To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the time consistency problem of mean variance portfolio selection can be solved by a local notion of efficiency; (2) a continuous time formulation of this problem can be obtained as a limit of a discrete time formulation; (3) the locally risk minimising strategy can be characterized by a global structure condition, which is also the limit of the corresponding structure condition in discrete time.

the mean variance portfolio selection problem can be formulated as a time consistent optimal control problem, which is well suited for a dynamic programming approach, and that the continuous time formulation can be justified by convergence results for the discrete time problem.

(1) the continuous time limit (as a sequence of discrete time models) of the local mean variance efficiency is the local mean variance efficient strategy in the continuous time model, and (2) this local mean variance efficient (time consistent) strategy is given in terms of the Follmer-Schweizer decomposition and the structure condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) What is the correct formulation of time consistent mean variance portfolio choice in discrete and continuous semimartingales? (2) How does this formulation arise from discrete time?
the following questions: What is a time consistent mean variance problem? What are its solutions? How can they be obtained? How can we justify the time consistent formulation?
the time consistency issue of mean variance portfolio selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the continuous time formulation is the correct one, which is in accordance with the continuous time formulation of the time inconsistent problem by Bjork Murgoci and Zhou (2012).

the continuous time formulation of the time consistent mean variance problem is a generalisation of the discrete time problem and that the Follmer and Schweizer decomposition is a generalisation for the discrete time problem.

we provide a new formulation of the time consistent mean variance portfolio problem in discrete and continuous semimartingales setting, we prove the convergence of the discrete formulation to the continuous one, and we show that the locally optimal strategy is given by the structure condition and Follmer Schweizers decomposition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time consistent mean variance portfolio problem in continuous time can be solved in the spirit of the discrete time approach by using the Follmer-Schweizer decomposition of the trade off.
the time consistent mean variance formulation can be obtained by taking the continuous time limit and then taking the local limit of the usual discrete time formulation.
we provide the first time consistent formulation of mean variance portfolio selection and its convergence in a general setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that

time consistent mean variance portfolio optimisation is a well defined problem, which is not Markovian in general and which can be treated in a general seminartingale setting using the structure condition.
, in the context of time inconsistent optimal control, it is not sufficient to impose the Markovian structure on the state process.

, even in continuous time, the time inconsistent nature of the mean variance problem does not prevent one from finding a natural time consistent formulation, which is based only on local notions of optimality.
